text: The Sanctum burned for three nights. When the relic shattered, the light that had ruled the realm for a thousand years went out like a candle in a crypt.
Across the land the other holy orders took up arms, but there was no Covenant left to lead them. The dead walked the pilgrim roads, and the living learned to bar their doors at dusk.
The necromancer did not sit the empty throne. Something else was calling the dead now, from far beneath the sea, and the army began to drift toward the coast.
The Eye's faithful had prayed for the Dreaming Mother to wake and claim every corpse as her vessel. They had not prayed for who would answer.
Vhal'Neth was dead long before her city sank, and the dead belong to the necromancer. The Eye's own ritual, sung by a thousand drowned throats, bound her to a new master.
Ul-Thalos sinks back beneath the waves. Somewhere far below, a god dreams of the necromancer's will, and the sea gives up its dead whenever it is asked.
The Covenant is ash. The Eye is blind. The army is endless, and it is only beginning.
The Empire had conquered death with steel. Its citizens were never buried; they were rebuilt, and rebuilt again, and called it forever.
In the Core of the Iron Citadel the god they built fell to its knees, and the necromancer reached into the broken engine for the one thing the Empire forgot to delete: Varn's soul.
Nothing is deathless. Everything is mine. Across the realm the machines went dark, rank after rank, and their founder rose to serve a new master.
Covenant, Eye and Empire are ash, blind and silent. The dead are the only empire left.
The army of the dead had grown so vast that the Underworld stood empty. Hades complained to Olympus that his kingdom was a desert, and the gods came down to take the dead back.
Their legions broke on the shore of Ilion, and one by one the gods of the mountain fell silent: Ares, Artemis, Poseidon, and at last Zeus himself.
Below the world, in the grey fields of asphodel, the Lord of the Dead rose from his throne to fight for what was his. Beaten, he did not die. He knelt, and laid his crown at the necromancer's feet.
The Styx runs again, and every soul it carries answers to one master. The gods are silent. The throne below is empty.
Act V: The Shogunate of the Rising Sun
With Olympus fallen there was only one day left for the dead to fear. Across the eastern sea a Shogun ruled in the sun goddess's name, and she had seen the night spreading west.
His armies sailed to burn it out. The dead met them in the burning rice fields, and the ninja of the Hidden Hand could not hide from them in any shadow.
Castle Kurogane fell regiment by regiment, until the Shogun came down from his platform and drew his own blade, and was cut down by the night.
On the road above the clouds the sun goddess crossed the sky one last time. When she fell, the sun went out. There will be no dawn again: only the night, and the dead who walk in it.
Far beyond the mountains, the holy orders the Covenant once led are lighting their beacons. They remember how to march, and they are marching on the dead.
Far below the world, the river of the dead has run dry, and its ferryman has no one left to carry. On a mountain of marble, the gods have noticed.
Olympus is silent and Hades kneels. Only one light still burns against the dead: across the eastern sea, a goddess opens her eyes.
The sun is out, and the night has no end. Far below, the souls owed to the Pit have stopped arriving, and something down there has started counting.
